items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Caesar Petrillo, and then he wrote back, “Don’t worry, go over there and tell them again.”

ctx.x: When we were still in Phoenix, we heard about the union, so we wanted to be members of the musicians’ union. We went over there to the headquarters of the musicians’ union in Phoenix, but they had no black members. We said we want to join the union, and they said no. Then we wrote letters back to the headquarters of the union

and to the president saying we want to join the union and they’re telling us we can’t join. I don’t remember whether we wrote to Chicago, Caesar Petrillo, and then he wrote back, “Don’t worry, go over there and tell them again.” So, we went over there to join, 586 in Phoenix. When we went to Los Angeles, the black local was 767, the white local was 47. We went to file our transfer, so we did. Guys were coming in. I saw Nat Cole there, Benny Carter, real big time people. If you come into the jurisdiction, you have…
Where was the office located? The black union office.
